strengths: The paper identifies a useful problem: interpretable macro-level features can be confounded with model predictions even when predictions are deterministic functions of pixels. This has an identifiable audience in causal discovery, explainability, and model auditing.

Applying FCI with the background knowledge that predictions cannot cause image features is a coherent approach under the stated assumptions. PAGs provide a useful language for distinguishing definite causes, possible causes, and confounded associations.

The geometric-shape simulation illustrates how omitting a relevant feature can make causal and associational explanations differ. The manuscript also provides substantial preprocessing and implementation details.

The exposition is generally accessible, and Sections 7.2–7.3 acknowledge important limitations concerning identification, background knowledge, and interpretable feature selection. A new algorithm or state-of-the-art predictive performance is unnecessary for this contribution.
weaknesses: Necessary: The empirical conclusions sometimes exceed what the reported graphs establish. Figure 8 pools directed and partially directed edges, although a partially directed edge remains compatible with pure confounding. Its bootstrap frequency therefore does not establish confidence that a feature is causal. Figures 9–10 and Section 6.4 nevertheless describe features as likely causes or important determinants. Conversely, absence of adjacency to the prediction does not establish causal irrelevance: an effect may be mediated by another observed feature. Report the edge types separately, consider ancestry through the full PAG, and revise these causal and noncausal conclusions accordingly.

Necessary: The X-ray sampling creates an unresolved selection problem. Section 6.1 selects 120 pneumonia cases and 120 controls with 'no findings,' making inclusion depend on diagnosis and the findings used as explanatory variables. This can introduce selection dependence, whereas Section 3 treats selection bias as irrelevant and the subsequent interpretations assume that setting. The analysis needs to account for this sampling mechanism, use an appropriate alternative sample, or withdraw the unsupported causal interpretation of this application.

Necessary: The reliability of the conditional-independence tests underlying the real-data results is insufficiently established. The birds analysis uses chi-square tests with multilevel variables and conditioning sets of up to four attributes; sparse contingency tables are a substantial concern with only a few thousand images. The X-ray analysis has just 240 images. Bootstrap stability does not itself establish test calibration or orientation accuracy. Specify which data splits supplied the FCI observations, explain sparse-cell handling, and establish that the principal conclusions are robust to reasonable testing choices. Otherwise, present these results as exploratory illustrations rather than validated causal explanations.

Necessary: The Shapley counterexample requires correction or a more precise definition of its estimands. Appendix A.2 declares Z3 omitted but leaves it fixed inside the prediction function while integrating over the marginal distribution of Z1 and Z2. This does not establish the claimed backdoor-adjustment calculation using only Z2; an observational calculation would need to account for the conditional distribution of the omitted variable. The comparison also changes the player set and baseline. Consequently, the asserted zero-versus-nonzero attribution example does not isolate confounding as claimed. Define the attribution games and available information explicitly, then rederive or replace the example.

Optional: Repeated synthetic trials and a comparison using the same macro-level annotations would strengthen the practical evaluation. The LIME and SHAP visualizations illustrate differences in explanatory units and local versus population-level targets, but do not independently validate the accuracy of the learned causal explanations. Broader benchmarking would be useful, rather than a prerequisite based on novelty or significance.
